title: Vancouver Trivia Night

questions.q: Vancouver co-hosted the Winter Olympics with Whistler in which year?
Vancouver hosted a world's fair, remembered by the name "Expo" and a two-digit year. Which year?
Stanley Park is named after the same Governor General as which famous trophy?
Which Vancouver neighbourhood takes its name from a talkative saloon keeper, John Deighton?
What is the name of Vancouver's NHL team?
What is the name of the CFL team that plays at BC Place?
Which suspension bridge carries traffic from Stanley Park across Burrard Inlet to the North Shore?
The city is named after a Royal Navy captain who charted this coast in 1792. What was his first name?
Which international environmental organization was founded in Vancouver in the early 1970s?
Which strait separates the Vancouver area from Vancouver Island?

notes: Vancouver 2010 Olympic Winter Games, co-hosted with Whistler; see Olympics.com / Wikipedia '2010 Winter Olympics'.
Expo 86 ran May to October 1986 in Vancouver; see Wikipedia 'Expo 86'.
Stanley Park (opened 1888) and the Stanley Cup are both named for Lord Stanley of Preston, Governor General; see Wikipedia 'Stanley Park' / 'Stanley Cup'.
Gastown is named for John 'Gassy Jack' Deighton, a talkative saloon keeper who arrived in 1867; see Wikipedia 'Gastown' / City of Vancouver.
Vancouver Canucks, NHL since 1970; see nhl.com/canucks / Wikipedia 'Vancouver Canucks'.
BC Lions play home games at BC Place; see bclions.com / Wikipedia 'BC Lions'.
Lions Gate Bridge (opened 1938) crosses the First Narrows of Burrard Inlet from Stanley Park to the North Shore; see Wikipedia 'Lions Gate Bridge'.
Named after Captain George Vancouver, who surveyed Burrard Inlet in 1792; see Wikipedia 'George Vancouver' / City of Vancouver history.

Greenpeace grew out of the Don't Make a Wave Committee formed in Vancouver in 1970, taking the Greenpeace name in 1971-72; see Wikipedia 'Greenpeace'. Question says 'early 1970s' to avoid the 1970/1971/1972 dispute.
The Strait of Georgia (part of the Salish Sea) lies between the Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island; see Wikipedia 'Strait of Georgia'. Accept 'the Salish Sea' or 'Georgia Strait'.
